thread:
Maya K: Incident page — Private VPC cluster for acme-corp (eu-west-1) reporting GPU node provisioning failures and large request queue. Customers seeing 503s and token throttling. Threading here to coordinate.
IncidentBot: SEV2 triggered by health-checks: autoscaler.failed_provision (acme-corp-vpc). Paging oncall now.
Oncall-Alex: I'm oncall, acknowledging. Assigning to infra/runtime. @samir @liz_h please triage.
Samir: Jumping in. High-level: autoscaler attempted to create 3 p4d-like nodes at 12:42 UTC, cloud API returned PROVISION_DELAY for node group, then provider quota returned ENI_LIMIT_EXCEEDED in logs. Autoscaler entered backoff and stopped creating nodes. Queue length ~1.2k requests, per-customer throttles kicking in.
Liz H: Copy. Can you paste the autoscaler events and node-provision logs? I'll check node-bootstrap daemonset status.
Samir: Logs excerpt:
```
[2026-06-14T12:42:11Z] autoscaler: scaleUp(3) -> provider.createNodeGroup -> error: EnqueueProvision: ENI_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
[2026-06-14T12:42:14Z] autoscaler: backoff until 2026-06-14T12:45:11Z
[2026-06-14T12:46:05Z] provisioner: node-init failed: timeout waiting for kubelet
```
Maya K: Customer success (Carl) just DM'd: multiple customers on acme-corp tenant experiencing failed inference jobs. They're asking ETA.
Carl: acme-corp ticket opened; customer mentions degraded SLAs and failing user flows. They want mitigation now.
Oncall-Alex: Immediate mitigations we should consider:
- Route acme-corp traffic to hosted fallback pool (rate-limited) — requires QA from product/solutions
- Force-scale a smaller GPU flavor present in VPC (if compatible) to get some capacity
- Increase autoscaler retries and temporarily disable backoff
- Open cloud provider ticket for ENI/quota
Which do we want now?
Mei: We can route some traffic to hosted, but acme-corp data policy blocks sending certain requests off-prem. We can offer partial routing for non-sensitive routes.
Ryan P: I can attempt a manual node create of a compatible `gpu-a100-40` flavor that doesn't require extra ENIs. If that fails, we fallback.
Samir: Trying manual create now with CLI:
```
redwood infra create-node --cluster acme-corp-vpc --flavor gpu-a100-40 --count 2 --labels=role=inference
```
Samir: CLI returned: ProvisionInitiated -> wait. Provider API shows pending nodes with status "NETWORK_WAIT".
Liz H: Checking node-bootstrap logs: daemonset `nv_inference-bootstrap` stuck on "Waiting for kernel modules" on two nodes that completed provisioning earlier. That's preventing kubelet registration. I'm exec'ing into bootstrap to restart.
Liz H: Ran `kubectl -n infra rollout restart ds/nv_inference-bootstrap` and `kubectl get nodes` shows one new node in NotReady, kubelet registering now.
Samir: One node became Ready at 12:58 UTC. Autoscaler still in backoff and won't attempt more until 13:05. Queue size dropped from 1200 -> 800 after we got one node.
Oncall-Alex: Good. Short term: restart autoscaler backoff to force another scale attempt. Ben, can you update autoscaler config to reduce backoff and trigger immediate scale-up? Leave a 15m guardrail.
Ben S: On it. Patched autoscaler config: `scaleDownDelay=300`, `scaleUpBackoff=30s` (temp). Triggering scaleUp probe.
Ben S: scaleUp probe triggered, provider accepted 2 more nodes. Provider returned `PROVISION_DELAY` for the first attempt, then `OK` on retry. New nodes provisioning.
IncidentBot: Noted change in autoscaler configuration. Please follow up with config rollback after incident.
Maya K: Customer-facing note: Carl, please tell acme-corp we have partial capacity restored and are routing non-sensitive workloads where allowed. ETA for full capacity depends on provider quota clearance; we'll aim for full restoration in 45-60 minutes. Documenting.
Carl: Sent update to customer. They asked for a postmortem and a timeline for preventing recurrence.
Samir: Cloud provider responded to a support case: ENI quota was near limit for that VPC due to a stale ENI leak from a prior test. Provider cleaned up 4 stale ENIs; quota now has headroom for 3 more GPU nodes.
Liz H: All three additional nodes are Ready now at 13:10 UTC. Queue down to 120, throttling reduced. No more 503 spikes in metrics dashboard.
Oncall-Alex: Good. Current impact: degraded throughput for ~28 minutes, partial request loss - customer-facing errors mostly mitigated. Moving to recovery state. Keeping SEV2 until verified for 1 hour.
Ryan P: Follow-ups I will own: (1) add ENI/leak detection to cluster health checks, (2) add quicker autoscaler retry path for on-prem provider errors.
Ben S: I'll revert temporary autoscaler backoff changes and create a canary config change to test shorter backoffs in non-prod. Also create an alert on "autoscaler backoff > 5m with queue > 100".
Maya K: Postmortem owner: Maya + Samir. Add timeline, root cause: provider ENI quota exhaustion + autoscaler backoff + node-bootstrap flakiness. Action items: provider quota monitoring, bootstrap restart automation, autoscaler retry tuning, customer fallback policy docs.
IncidentBot: SEV2 marked: mitigation in progress -> monitoring. Please add postmortem link when ready.
Oncall-Alex: Handing off to night oncall in 2 hours; will file a runbook note in incidents/wiki and ping infra on pager duty.
Mei: I will coordinate with Solutions Eng to prepare an opt-in hosted-fallback flow for customers with data exemptions.
Carl: Customer acknowledged update; they requested timeframe for PM and SLA credits if applicable.
Maya K: Noted. I'll draft post-incident customer note.
Samir: Final check at 13:25 UTC: CPU/GPU utilization normalized, queue < 20, no 5xx errors in last 5m.
Oncall-Alex: Closing real-time mitigation. Keeping thread open for postmortem comments.

Summary lines (for postmortem):
- Incident start: 2026-06-14T12:42:11Z
- Mitigations: manual node create; restart bootstrap DS; adjust autoscaler backoff; provider cleared ENI leak; traffic partial reroute where permitted.
- Impact: ~28m degraded throughput, partial request failures for acme-corp.
- Owners: Maya K (PM/inci lead), Samir (runtime), Liz H (infra), Ben S (autoscaler), Mei (solutions), Carl (CS)

Next steps: write postmortem, add monitoring checks for ENI leaks and autoscaler stuck backoff, automate bootstrap restarts, document hosted-fallback policy for private clusters.
